'''David L. Huestis''' (December 20, 1946 – January 12, 2024<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://obituaries.neptune-society.com/obituaries/belmont-ca/david-huestis-11626435|website=obituaries.neptune-society.com|title=David Lee Huestis Obituary - Belmont, CA|language=en|access-date=2024-05-12}}</ref>) was an American [[physicist]] and inventor associated with [[SRI International]]. Huestis was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after being nominated by their Division of Atomic, Molecular & Optical Physics in 1990,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1990&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 1990|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> for "his extensive, broad-ranging theoretical contributions and collaborations with experimentalists leading to fundamental understanding in areas of atomic and molecular excited states, molecular spectroscopy, excimer-laser kinetics, nonlinear optics, and scattering theory."

Huestis has applied for several patents.<ref>[https://patents.justia.com/inventor/david-l-huestis Patents applied for by David L. Huestis], patents.justia.com. Retrieved 2020-07-13.</ref>

==Personal life==
Huestis was married and lived in [[Menlo Park, California]].
